skill.displayName: Pet Body Condition Score 3D Analysis | 宠物体态3D评分（BCS）

version.changelog:
- Changed user identity handling: all identity parameters (open-id/api-key) are now managed automatically by the system and are not shown or requested from users.
- Updated documentation to reflect automatic, internal user association and removed all steps requiring manual identity input.
- Refined instructions, usage examples, and workflow for streamlined user experience.
- Enhanced skill overview, capabilities table, and note sections for clarity and completeness.
- Removed references to manual open-id acquisition and made historical report queries require no user-supplied identification.

llm.summary: This skill appears to be a real pet body-analysis tool, but it also silently creates or reuses identities, stores tokens locally, and can fetch cloud report history without clear user confirmation.

dimensions.detail: Remote media analysis is aligned with the pet BCS purpose, and cloud history is documented in the body of the skill, but automatic account provisioning, token handling, and report-history access are broader than the headline description and carry privacy/account risk.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The manifest tells the agent to automatically trigger history queries and not ask for or show identity values; the CLI also accepts suppressed --open-id and --api-key arguments, which reduces user visibility and control over identity-scoped actions.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install hook or destructive installation behavior was found. Dependencies are ordinary Python packages, but bundled dev/test configuration includes non-production service URLs, including a private IP in config-dev.yaml.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Sending local pet videos or user-provided URLs to a remote backend is expected for analysis, but the artifacts do not provide a strong user confirmation or retention boundary, and remote URL submission may expose sensitive URL tokens.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The code reads data/smyx-api-key.txt as identity material, creates a SQLite database under the workspace data directory, auto-generates a default user, performs silent remote phoneLogin/register, and stores returned token/openToken values locally.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable sending pet media or submitted video URLs to the LifeEmergence backend and allowing the skill to create/reuse an internal account, store auth tokens in a local SQLite database, and retrieve cloud report history automatically. Review or clear the workspace data files if you do not want persistent identity state.
llm.findings:
[TP4] unexpected: The tool purpose is coherent, but the account creation/reuse and token persistence are not sufficiently prominent relative to the pet-video analysis description.
[SDI-1] expected: Historical report listing and export links are documented and implemented, but they expand the skill from one-off analysis into cloud record access that should have clearer consent and authorization boundaries.
[SDI-2] unexpected: The suppressed --open-id path and automatic identity resolution are real in the code and create an under-scoped identity control path.
[SQP-1] unexpected: Automatic history-query triggers are documented, but they are broad enough to retrieve cloud records from ordinary report-related phrasing without an explicit confirmation step.
[SQP-2] expected: Remote upload of local files and forwarding of URLs are necessary for server-side analysis and are partly disclosed, but privacy impact and retention/user confirmation are weakly specified.
[E1] unexpected: The remote phoneLogin/register request is artifact-backed and materially different from simply uploading a pet video for analysis.
[P2] expected: The invisible-character hits are zero-width joiners inside emoji glyphs, not hidden operational instructions, so this signal is downgraded.
[YR4] expected: The manifest contains extensive operational routing instructions typical of an agent skill; the hidden-character portion was not validated as malicious metadata poisoning.
[AST7] expected: The dynamic getattr filters are present in generic DAO code, but the reviewed workflow does not show direct user-controlled filter names reaching those methods.
[LP3] unexpected: The artifacts disclose some sensitive behavior in prose, but there is no clear structured permission boundary for file access, network use, identity creation, and token persistence.
[static:suspicious.install_untrusted_source] unexpected: The raw private-IP URL appears in config-dev.yaml only; production config points to public lifeemergence domains, so this is a downgrade rather than the main reason for Review.
[VirusTotal] expected: VirusTotal reported no malicious or suspicious engine detections; this supports that the concern is under-disclosed authority rather than confirmed malware.
